images.title: Left side matches right side
images.purpose: Show that a symmetric picture has one side matching the other, and a cloud does not.
images.composition: Two outlines side by side with wide space between them, each with a dotted vertical line.
images.exact_structure: Left: a simple flat outline of the Taj Mahal with one central dome and 2 equal towers on each side, one dotted vertical line down the exact middle, left half tinted teal #0072B2 and right half tinted amber #E69F00, the two sides exact mirror images. Right: one cloud outline with an uneven shape, a dotted vertical line down its middle, both sides plain and clearly different. Exactly 2 pictures, 2 dotted lines.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a cloud with matching sides, or a Taj Mahal with unequal sides
images.takeaway: A picture is symmetrical when one side matches the other.
images.description: A Taj Mahal outline with a middle dotted line and mirror matching tinted halves, next to a cloud outline whose two sides differ.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at a tower on the left and find the matching tower on the right.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
